everything works ok. 

Due to this, a check for existence and removal of names in the geometry column should therefore be implemented, probably  in `normalize-sf.R`

(See also https://stackoverflow.com/questions/53227205/polygons-not-getting-plotted-in-leaflet-r-map-since-update and https://github.com/r-spatial/sf/issues/880#issuecomment-435304536)

title: addPolygons/addMarkers only draws first row of SF data.frame, issue disappears when layerId is omitted
description:
I'm using the github versions of both **leaflet** and **leaflet.extras**

I have the following leaflet code: 

```r
leaflet(width = "100%", height = "100%") %>%
      setView(4.3517103,50.8503396,10) %>%
      addTiles(group = "OpenStreetMap", urlTemplate = "http://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png") %>%

      addProviderTiles("Stamen.Toner", group = "High contrast") %>%

      addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery", group = "Satellite") %>%

       addDrawToolbar(
        targetGroup='Selection',
         polylineOptions = FALSE,
          circleOptions = FALSE,
        markerOptions = FALSE,
        editOptions = editToolbarOptions()
        ) %>%

      addLayersControl(
        baseGroups = c("High contrast", "OpenStreetMap", "Satellite"),
        options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = TRUE, autoZIndex = TRUE)
```

Based on the area selected with the drawing of leaflet.draw, my code selects polygons /point geometries from different shapefiles (propietary data, cannot share), represented in R as SF data.frames. I can see that the code selects multiple rows (as it should), because the selections have 10+ rows, but only the first row of each data.frame is showing up on the map when I use a leaflet Proxy (and for-loop, for the polygons) to add them to the map:

```r
layers <- c()

      prox <-  leafletProxy("map", session, deferUntilFlush=TRUE) 
      prox %>%
        clearMarkers() %>%
        clearShapes() %>%
       addMarkers( data=setToPlot()$antennas, layerId = "layer_Antennas", group="Antennas")  
        
      for (i in names(setToPlot()$polygons)) {
        
        write(paste(i,"/", nrow(setToPlot()$polygons[[i]])), stderr())
        if(nrow(setToPlot()$polygons[[i]]) > 0) {
          prox  %>%
            addPolygons(data=setToPlot()$polygons[[i]],
                             layerId = paste0("layer_",i), group=i, dashArray = NULL)
          layers <- c(layers, i)
        }
        
      }
      
      prox %>%
        removeLayersControl() %>%
        addLayersControl(
          baseGroups = c("High contrast", "OpenStreetMap", "Satellite"),
          overlayGroups = c("Selection", "Antennas", layers),
          options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = TRUE, autoZIndex = TRUE)
        )  
```

I've found a similar issue on stackoverflow (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/51275767/only-the-first-polygon-is-showing-up-in-leaflet-2-0-1-choropleth-plot), where the suggested solution is to add "dashArray = NULL" to the addPolygons call, but this does not solve the problem.

In my tests, the issue goes away when I **omit** the  layerId argument. This is the case even for simpler leaflet maps, such as 


-  Will plot all markers/rows in data.frame
```r
leaflet(setToPlot()$antennas) %>%
addTiles() %>%
addMarkers()
```
- Will only plot first row
```r
leaflet(setToPlot()$antennas) %>%
addTiles() %>%
addMarkers(layerId="antennas")
```

title: scales 1.0.0 change to colour_ramp to cause test failure
description:
The upcoming scales 1.0.0 release has a minor change to the default settings and output of the `scales::colour_ramp()` function, introduced by r-lib/scales#109. This change sets the default `alpha = TRUE` and changes the output so that fully opaque colors are returned in  `"#RRGGBB"` format.

During our revdep checks, it seems that this change breaks a colors test for `leaflet`, speficifically the test starting at [L39 in the test-colors.r file](https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/blob/eaee4d55ff59e6885ac6559778633cec57d0729a/tests/testit/test-colors.R#L39)

The error output is below:

```
Error from assert(identical(c("#000000", "#7F7F7F", "#FFFFFF"), colorNumeric(colorRamp(bw),  ...  at test-colors.R#34 
Error: identical(c("#000000FF", "#777777FF", "#FFFFFFFF", "#FFFFFF00", "blue"), colorNumeric(c(bw, "#FFFFFF00"),  ....  is not TRUE
Execution halted
```
Just wanted to give the maintainers a heads up. We expect to release shortly but don't expect this to be a breaking change to plots. Let me know if I can offer more clarity about the change.

title: support for ESRI Arctic Ocean Base map (polar stereo projection)
description:
I have been searching for a viable solution that would allow use of leaflet (and, also, mapview) with points, lines, polygons and rasters that cross the 180 longitude line. I have long hoped for a reliable, simple solution based on web mercator. But, I've yet to find anything satisfactory.

Leaflet's support of additional projections is a great solution except for the lack of tile options available. That said, ESRI has recently released [Arctic Ocean Basemap](http://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=c7381cb155a043a2bba2b84566677262) which is in the Alaska Polar Stereographic projection. 

I've managed to sort out all the parameter details for the `tile_url` and `leafletCRS` function. Here, I present an example that others who are interested in the US Arctic may find useful. 

I would also be interested in how I might contribute this to either leaflet or, maybe leaflet-providers or leaflet-extras, so the full configuration doesn't have to be specified each time. I imagine something similar could be specified for ArcticConnect and other tile sources (e.g. Antarctica).

``` r
library(leaflet)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
library(sf)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
#> Linking to GEOS 3.6.2, GDAL 2.2.4, proj.4 5.0.1
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
track_line <-                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
'LINESTRING (-169.4444 62.57549, -169.8999 62.31869, -170.4738 62.16436, -170.6529 61.4344, -171.7103 60.5111, -173.5295 60.78438, -175.2325 61.55942, -176.0107 61.88525, -177.1819 61.43621, -177.3077 61.25797, -177.3493 61.98553, -176.4385 62.26207, -177.3228 62.73083, -179.2457 62.84639, 179.7168 62.67369, 179.8549 62.58532, 179.8978 62.60145, -179.7893 62.64932, 179.9897 62.37538, -179.6393 62.66016, -179.8876 62.60982, -179.68 62.75012, 179.8264 62.78815, -179.789 62.72092, 179.6381 62.48176)'
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
track_line <- sf::st_as_sfc(track_line) %>%                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
sf::st_set_crs(4326)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
tile_url <- 'https://services.arcgisonline.com/arcgis/rest/services/Polar/Arctic_Ocean_Base/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}.png'                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
origin <- c(-2.8567784109255e+07, 3.2567784109255e+07)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
minZoom <- 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
maxZoom <- 24                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
resolutions <- c(                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
238810.813354,119405.406677, 59702.7033384999, 29851.3516692501,14925.675834625,
7462.83791731252,3731.41895865639, 1865.70947932806,932.854739664032,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
466.427369832148, 233.213684916074, 116.60684245803701, 58.30342122888621,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
29.151710614575396, 14.5758553072877, 7.28792765351156, 3.64396382688807,
1.82198191331174, 0.910990956788164, 0.45549547826179, 0.227747739130895,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
0.113873869697739, 0.05693693484887, 0.028468467424435                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
epsg5936 <- leafletCRS(                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
crsClass = 'L.Proj.CRS',                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
code = 'EPSG:5936',                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
proj4def = '+proj=stere +lat_0=90 +lat_ts=90 +lon_0=-150 +k=0.994 +x_0=2000000 +y_0=2000000 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs',                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
origin = origin,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
resolutions = resolutions                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
leaflet(track_line,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
options= leafletOptions(                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
crs=epsg5936)) %>%                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
addTiles(urlTemplate = tile_url,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
attribution = "Esri, DeLorme, GEBCO, NOAA NGDC, and other contributors",                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
options = tileOptions(minZoom = 0, maxZoom = 24)) %>%                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
addPolylines()                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
```

title: Expose Leaflet.js panes
description:
from @tim-salabim in #535 ...

..., we have freshly implemented a method to create custom map panes in a leaflet map following [this tutorial](http://leafletjs.com/examples/map-panes/). The relevant js code is [here](https://github.com/r-spatial/mapview/blob/develop/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/pane/map-pane.js) and the R functions are [here](https://github.com/r-spatial/mapview/blob/develop/R/extensions.R#L970-L988). 
I think this is general enough to have this in leaflet rather than mapview and I am more than happy to migrate this over for the next CRAN release (until then, I'd prefer to keep it in mapview, where it will be part of the next CRAN release). 
Let me know if you are interested in migrating this to leaflet.

For completeness, [here](https://github.com/r-spatial/mapview/blob/develop/R/mapviewControls.R#L272-L286) is where we specify the panes for use in mapview such that by default points overlay lines overlay polygons.

title: allow options for addRasterImage
description:
Thanks for the recent update! It really brings some great new features. One feature I have been exploiting is map pane definition to control layer order in a map, e.g. points always on top of polygons. 

This works great:

```r
library(leaflet)
library(mapview) # for the data

leaflet() %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addPolygons(data = franconia, 
              group = "polygons",
              opacity = 1,
              fillOpacity = 1,
              options = leafletOptions(pane = "tilePane")) %>%
  addCircleMarkers(data = breweries,
                   group = "points",
                   color = "black",
                   fillColor = "black",
                   options = leafletOptions(pane = "overlayPane")) %>%
  addLayersControl(overlayGroups = c("polygons", "points"))
```
However, this does not work for `addRasterImage` (throughing error `unused argument (options = leafletOptions(pane = "overlayPane"))`). 

```r
leaflet() %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addRasterImage(poppendorf[[4]], 
                 project = TRUE,
                 options = leafletOptions(pane = "overlayPane"))
```
If I understand correctly, `addRasterImage` uses `L.GridLayer` for the image rendering which has an [option to specify the pane.](http://leafletjs.com/reference-1.3.0.html#gridlayer-pane)

It would be great of we could add an `options` argument to `addRasterImage` so we can define which pane it should be rendered in. There are situations where you'd want an image to overlay vector features.

Related to this, we have freshly implemented a method to create custom map panes in a leaflet map following [this tutorial](http://leafletjs.com/examples/map-panes/). The relevant js code is [here](https://github.com/r-spatial/mapview/blob/develop/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/pane/map-pane.js) and the R functions are [here](https://github.com/r-spatial/mapview/blob/develop/R/extensions.R#L970-L988). 
I think this is general enough to have this in leaflet rather than mapview and I am more than happy to migrate this over for the next CRAN release (until then, I'd prefer to keep it in mapview, where it will be part of the next CRAN release). 
Let me know if you are interested in migrating this to leaflet.

For completeness, [here](https://github.com/r-spatial/mapview/blob/develop/R/mapviewControls.R#L272-L286) is where we specify the panes for use in mapview such that by default points overlay lines overlay polygons.

Thanks again for the great work you've put into leaflet recently!!

But I would prefer a solution with leaflet and it was recommended I ask this group. Any advice would be greatly appreciated. 

Here is my sample data:

df <- data.frame(

  "International" =  c("Auckland", "Bandar Seri Begawan", "Bangkok", "Christchurch", "Denpasar", "Dunedin", "Hamilton", "Hong Kong", "Honiara", "Kuala Lumpur"),

)
```

library(rgeos)

library(shiny)

title: addLegend and NA work but only with a workaround
description:
Providing `addLegend` with values in the fashion `values = df$variable` rather than `values =~variable` solves an occurrence of the error: 
```
Error in UseMethod("metaData") : 
  no applicable method for 'metaData' applied to an object of class "NULL"
```
which happens if `variable` has NA's.

I don't see why isn't this the default behaviour. 

source:
https://stackoverflow.com/a/32011289/3494126


p.s. for instance, just following [this official tutorial ](https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/legends.html) with my data I produced the abovementioned error. 

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Ok, @jcheng5 thanks for the explanation, now I can produce a working/non-working example:


```R
library(leaflet)
library(sf)

N = 10
center = c(16.37, 48.21)  # Vienna approx center
random_event = list()
random_event$lat = rnorm(N, center[1], sd = 0.001)
random_event$lon = rnorm(N, center[2], sd = 0.001)
random_event = as.data.frame(random_event)
random_event = st_as_sf(random_event, coords = c('lat', 'lon'), crs = 4326)

random_event$random_intensity = rbinom(N, 5, 0.4)

pal = colorFactor('Greens', domain = random_event$random_intensity)

leaflet_plot = (

    leaflet() %>%
    addProviderTiles(leaflet::providers$CartoDB.Positron) %>%
    addCircles(
        data = random_event$geometry,
        weight = 2, opacity = 0.5, color = pal(random_event$random_intensity),
        radius = 5.5, fill = T
    )
    %>%
    addLegend('bottomright',
        pal = pal,
        # values = random_event$random_intensity,  # works fine
        values = ~random_intensity   # doesn't work
    )

)
print(leaflet_plot)
```

Indeed, the mistake here is using `leaflet() %>%` instead of `leaflet(random_event) %>%` which then works with both versions. 

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I still thing this is a minor bug. But feel free to disregard it. I will try to improve the SO issue, so that anyone who does the same in the future understands why it is not a bug. Although, with your explanation it is definitely more informative.

title: Is there a reason to default on `ordered=FALSE` in colorFactor?
description:
It took me quite some time (1-2 hours) to pinpoint a color mismatch problem, which was caused by calling `colorFactor` with a color palette and a character vector. The character vector was sorted again in converting into factors.

> ordered | If TRUE and domain needs to be coerced to a factor, treat it as already in the correct order

I can't think of a reason to use `ordered=FALSE` by default. We are supplying a color palette and a character vector and relying on order of them here. If the character vector should be sorted by name, it's better to let user sort it explicitly before calling `colorFactor`. 

I have sorted my character vector according to other value, then it got sorted by name implicitly and messed up the order.

title: Tilelayers over HTTPS
description:
Most providers have the protocol hardcoded in to the URL:

`"url": "http://{s}.basemaps.cartocdn.com/{variant}/{z}/{x}/{y}.png"`

Which throws mixed content errors to the console when loading using SSL:

You could just go with protocol less/relative URL like some providers already have:

`"url": "//{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png",`

but that is considered an antipattern since there is no way of forcing SSL when you need it, so it would need a new option, something like this:

`"url": "{protocol}://{s}.basemaps.cartocdn.com/{variant}/{z}/{x}/{y}.png"`

I'de love to do a PR for you but i'm very unfamiliar with R

title: Absolute Path Dependencies
description:
In my use case, I'm displaying a Leaflet Map R Object created in one environment in a Shiny dashboard in a different environment. There is considerably processing that happens to create the Leaflet Map R Object, which is not suitable for the dashboard deployment environment.

In `plugin-providers.R` and other files the absolute paths of the dependencies (e.g. `/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.4/Resources/library/leaflet/htmlwidgets/lib/leaflet-providers`) are written into the object:
```R
leafletProviderDependencies <- function() {
  list(
    htmltools::htmlDependency(
      "leaflet-providers",
      "1.0.27",
      system.file("htmlwidgets/lib/leaflet-providers", package = "leaflet"),
      script = "leaflet-providers.js"
    ),
    ....
}
```

Trying to load a map object created on one platform on different platform produces errors like the following:
```
Error in normalizePath: path[1]="/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.4/Resources/library/leaflet/htmlwidgets/lib/leaflet-providers": No such file or directory
Stack trace (innermost first):
    83: h
    82: .handleSimpleError
    81: normalizePath
    80: addResourcePath
    79: FUN
    78: lapply
    77: origRenderFunc
    76: output$scores_map
    75: ..stacktraceon..
...
     1: runApp
```

To prevent this error, store the relative path of the dependency rather than the absolute path. Currently, my work-around when loading a saved map object looks like (this is not a good solution, but works for my needs):
```R
data("my_map.Rda") # reads in my_map, a stored Leaflet Map Object
# fix an isssue where these dependencies are hard coded in the stored R objects
my_map$dependencies[[1]]$src$file <- normalizePath(paste0(.libPaths()[1], "/leaflet/htmlwidgets/lib/leaflet-providers"))
my_map$dependencies[[2]]$src$file <- normalizePath(paste0(.libPaths()[1], "/leaflet/htmlwidgets/plugins/leaflet-providers-plugin"))
```

Thanks!

description:

The output is correctly rendered in the RStudio Viewer, just not the browser (Chrome/Firefox). Polygons and polylines both render correctly in both the browser and viewer, just the CircleMarkers don't.

Code snippet example as follows
```
leaflet() %>% 
  addProviderTiles("CartoDB.Positron") %>%
  addCircleMarkers(data = cases, group = "Cases", radius = ~hh_scale * 4, stroke = TRUE, color = "grey40", 
weight =1.5, fill = TRUE, fillColor = ~pal(wksago), fillOpacity = 0.75, popup = ~label ) %>%
  addPolylines(data = boundaries, color = "#2e6568", weight = 3, smoothFactor = 1, group="Boundaries") %>%

title: NA values are repeatedly added in linked legend when switching layer off/on
description:
First of all many thanks for the grouped layer/legend feature. This really is a game changer as it makes interacting with the map much cleaner. I found a little bug related to NA value rendering in the legend.

If we use the new `group` argument in `addLegend` and the data has NAs I see that the `na.color` part of the legend gets repeatedly added to the legend as the layer is switched on/off. 

```r
library(leaflet)
library(mapview)
library(sf)

breweries = st_join(breweries, franconia[, "district"])

pal = colorFactor(c("red", "purple", "blue"), 
                  domain = mapview::breweries$district, 
                  na.color = "#BEBEBE")

leaflet() %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(data = breweries, color = ~pal(district), group = "breweries")  %>%
  addLayersControl(overlayGroups = "breweries") %>%
  addLegend(pal = pal, values = breweries$district, group = "breweries")
```
In the primary rendering of the legend everything looks as expected. If we switch the `breweries` layer off and on we get a second `NA` entry in the legend. This is repeatedly added every time we switch the layer off/on.

title: Feature Request: Support for addLegend in a leafletProxy() pipeline
description:
It would be convenient to update the legend within a leafletProxy pipeline as different datasets are added.

This makes most sense where you are switching between datasets shown in a map, or against a categorical variable in your data. However, here's a cheap example use case using `quakes`

```r
shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(wellPanel(uiOutput("depth_slider_UI")),
                 leafletOutput("my_map")),
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$depth_slider_UI <- renderUI({
      sliderInput(
        "quake_depth",
        "Depth",
        min = 40,
        max = 100,
        value = 50
      )
      
    })
    
    observeEvent(input$quake_depth,
                 {
                   my_quakes <- quakes %>%
                     filter(depth <= input$quake_depth)
                   
                   pal_quakes <- colorNumeric("Purples", quakes$mag)
                   
                   leafletProxy("my_map") %>%
                     clearMarkers() %>%
                     addCircleMarkers(
                       data = my_quakes,
                       stroke = TRUE,
                       fillColor = ~ pal_quakes(mag),
                       color = "#000000"
                     ) %>%
                     addLegend(pal = pal_quakes,
                               values = my_quakes$mag,
                               opacity = 1)
                   
                 })
    
    output$my_map <- renderLeaflet({
      leaflet() %>%
        addTiles()
      
    })
    
  }
)
```

title: leafletProxy stops working after renderUI changes leaflet dimensions
description:
I'm having some funny behavior with leafletProxy and renderUI. I want to be able to resize the leaflet map by user input, however after resizing, leafletProxy doesn't do anything and sometimes I get this message in the browser console: 

`Couldn't find map with id map1`

See below for a slightly modified leafletProxy example reprex that includes this resizing ability. You can click on a marker to remove it, until you resize the map using the slider, then leafletProxy no longer does anything.

``` r
library(shiny)
library(leaflet)

ui <- fluidPage(
  sliderInput("mapWidth", "Map Width", 2.5, 97.5, 50),
  uiOutput("rootUI")
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$rootUI <- renderUI({
    req(input$mapWidth)
    leafletOutput("map1", width = paste0(input$mapWidth, "%"))
  })
  output$map1 <- renderLeaflet({
    leaflet() %>%
      addCircleMarkers(lng = runif(10),
                       lat = runif(10),
                       layerId = paste0("marker", 1:10))
  })
  observeEvent(input$map1_marker_click, {
    leafletProxy("map1", session) %>%
      removeMarker(input$map1_marker_click$id)
  })
}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

I've seen similar questions asked with shinydashboard and that console warning, `Couldn't find map with id map1`, however I wasn't able to solve this issue by using the suggested `outputOptions(output, "map1", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)`.

I am using the latest development versions of shiny and leaflet.

Please let me know if I am trying to do something bad in shiny, and whether this should be done with JavaScript instead?

Thanks so much for the awesome package!
Hayden

title: Assign multiple layerIds to group.
description:
Hi,

I would like to be able to assign multiple layerIds to a group rather than have to duplicate the same layer every time I want it to be part of a group. 

For example, I want to create three groups: "All Locations", "Loop", and "River North." "All Locations" has two layers in it and "Loop" and "River North" have one layer each.

Current Implementation: 

```r
map <- addPolygons(map, data = temp.loop.spdf, fillColor = ~temp.gary(eligibles_adj),group = "All Locations")  
map <- addPolygons(map, data = temp.river.spdf, fillColor = ~temp.gary(eligibles_adj),group = "All Locations") 
map <- addPolygons(map, data = temp.loop.spdf, fillColor = ~temp.gary(eligibles_adj),group = "Loop")  
map <- addPolygons(map, data = temp.river.spdf, fillColor = ~temp.gary(eligibles_adj),group = "River North") 
```

Ideal Implementation: 

```r
map <- addPolygons(map, data = temp.loop.spdf, fillColor = ~temp.gary(eligibles_adj),layerId = "Loop")  
map <- addPolygons(map, data = temp.river.spdf, fillColor = ~temp.gary(eligibles_adj),layerId = "River North") 

createGroup(group_name = "All Locations", layerIds = c("Loop","River North")
createGroup(group_name = "Loop", layerIds = c("Loop")
createGroup(group_name = "River North", layerIds = c("River North")
```

Thanks for your assistance!

description:
Hi there, 

Using this [Gapminder example](https://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/215948_95c1ab86ad334d2f82856d9e5ebc16af.html), I attempted to connect a SpatialPolygonDataFrame on a leaflet map to its underlying dataframe (displayed in a datatable) using the `crosstalk` and `DT` packages. 

I get the following error: **Error in inherits(x, "SharedData") : attempt to apply non-function** when trying to reproduce the Gapminder example. 
The line that is causing the error is `sd$transform(as.data.frame)`. 
I have a feeling I may need to update something somewhere..


If you copy and paste this code it should replicate the error I am getting. 
```
library(leaflet)

library(rgdal)

proj4string(dub) <- CRS("+init=epsg:29902")

bscols(

title: Actual R version required at least R 3.3.0
description:
Based on this [Stack Overflow Question](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/43215120/error-in-leafletproxy-could-not-find-function-startswith), it appears that the leaflet package uses the [startsWith() function](https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/blob/ab565412ee53e736ba69c883c66856cacf9d3ed7/R/utils.R#L155) but that function did not appear [till R 3.3.0](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/NEWS.html). However the package lists "Depends: R (≥ 3.1.0)" in the [DESCRIPTION file](https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/blob/master/DESCRIPTION#L39).

Either a different function should be used or the required R version should be increased.

description:

The API key is used as a suffix like so: `https://{s}.tile.thunderforest.com/{variant}/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?apikey={apikey}`. I understand that the `providerTileOptions` function allows for some arguments to be passed to the tile API, but I cannot seem to successfully pass the API key. ```
# Create an empty map with thunderforest tiles
leaflet() %>% 
  addProviderTiles(providers$Thunderforest.Outdoors, 
    options = providerTileOptions(apikey = "mykey"))
```

Is there an undocumented way to pass the API key in this example? Thanks.

title: label formula fails when using crosstalk
description:
Labels can't be specified as formulas when the map data is a crosstalk SharedData. Simple example:

```
library(crosstalk)
library(leaflet)

shared_quakes <- SharedData$new(quakes[sample(nrow(quakes), 100),])
map = leaflet(shared_quakes,) %>% addTiles() %>% 
  addMarkers(label=~as.character(depth))
```

gives error

```
Error in UseMethod("metaData") : 
  no applicable method for 'metaData' applied to an object of class "c('SharedData', 'R6')"
```

The problem is a simple mis-spelling at line 2 of `normalize-SharedData.R`. `metaData.sharedData` should be `metaData.SharedData`.

title: ControlStore issues
description:
I discovered that many/all of the old `controls` do not use the implemented [`ControlStore`](https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/blob/master/javascript/src/control-store.js) mechanism.  I am happy to fix this and will submit a pull.

However, I believe the `add`/`remove` mechanisms are incomplete, since `controls` without `id` are added but cannot be removed with `ControlStore`.  In these [lines](https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/blob/master/javascript/src/control-store.js#L22-L26), only controls with initial `id` can be removed.  I believe since `leaflet` stamps all controls, we should in the add method also `push` the no-id `control` to `this._controlsById` once leaflet has stamped it.  Then, the `remove` method will work as expected.

title: Value for radius assumes largest value
description:
Hi

The code below draws a map with two airports.

The addCircleMarkers uses the airports_df such that the label is based on the IATA value, the popup on the Name value, and a calculation on the total_departures for the radius, which is also shown in the popup for debug purposes.

The resulting map shows the radius of the circles to be identical, and the value for the sqrt(total_departures) in the popup is also the same. This is wrong, as the value of total_departures for NHT is 0, so the formula should return 10 for the radius

What actually happens is that the value of sqrt(527) is being used for both circles.

Since the text for the popup and labels is correct, the correct row is being used for each circle marker, but not the correct value for total_departures.

I suspect that my syntax is wrong in some subtle way, but I can't see how. 

Help please?

Many thanks

Nathan

```
rm(list=ls())
require("leaflet")
require("dplyr")
Name <- c("London Heathrow Airport", "RAF Northolt")
IATA <- c("LHR", "NHT")
Lat <- c(as.numeric(51.4706), as.numeric(51.5530014038))
Long <- c(as.numeric(-0.461941), as.numeric(-0.418166995049))
total_departures <- c(527, 0)
airports_df <- data.frame(Name, IATA, Lat, Long, total_departures, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
str(airports_df)
airports_map_circles <- leaflet() %>% addTiles() %>% 
  addCircleMarkers(data = airports_df, popup = ~paste(Name, " - ", max(sqrt(total_departures), 10), sep = ""), label = ~IATA, clusterOptions = markerClusterOptions(), color = "purple", radius = ~max(sqrt(total_departures), 10)) 
airports_map_circles
```

title: Upgrade LeafletJS to 1.x
description:
## The issue

Now that LeafletJS 1.x has been out and stable for a while, it's time to think about upgrading to it. However it's not as simple and as straight forward as it sounds, so I'm creating this issue to capture all information related to the upgrade.

## Initial Assessment

The first order of thing is to adapt any existing code to use 1.x API, and the good news is that not much has changed, so most of the code can work as is. The only two things I am aware of are

- L.circle now accepts radius as an option (like L.circleMarker) rather than a second argument
- Labels are not supported by the Leaflet.label plugin anymore, rather they are incorporated in the core dist. and renamed to L.Tooltip

These are both minor changes can can be done only on the JS side w/o having to rewrite the R API.

Now for the hard parts.

The hardest part is going to be upgrading the plugins used. As plugins are individual contributions, it is up to the plugin author to migrate to 1.x and unfortunately not all have done so. We need to review this on a case by case basis. Starting with Proj4Leaflet which is critical in supporting custom projections. Proj4Leaflet hasn't been fully migrated to 1.x, but a branch does exists claiming to support 1.x. The problem is that the maintainer of Proj4Leaflet has not found spare time to work on it in a while and the branch is > 6 months old.

Next are some other plugins we use in the package such as AwesomeMarkers, Measure, Minimap, Terminator, omnivore, leaflet-providers, Easybutton, marker cluster, location filter (for crosstalk).
 The repos of all these plugins needs to be examined and we need to determine what efforts will require for each of them.

Lastly we have the leaflet sup-packages, starting with leaflet.extras (by your's truly), and mapview. These two use a lot of leaflet plugins and they too must be examined for the level of efforts required.

## The benefits

- 0.7 branch is no longer being developed or fixed.
- 1.x branch has a lot of performance and bug fixes.
- 1.x has support for some really cool stuff like vector tiles, webgl and more.
- Always pays off to stay current.

## Action Plan

- I can take a first stab at porting just the leaflet package (along with any plugins it uses) to 1.x
- For preventing any compatibility issues I will call this package leaflet2 (leaflet2 which is based on LeafletJS 1.x, I know how ironic that sounds).
- Once this is in a usable condition, I'll begin to work on leaflet.extras and more.

@jcheng5 @hadley @timelyportfolio @tim-salabim @mdsumner Please provide your inputs on this. This is quite critical in keeping the package up to date and viable for the coming years. 

One thing you guys can help out immediately is discussing whether this needs to be a new package (leaflet2), or simply continue with the same name. I don't think compatibility is going to be an issue for users of just this packge, but for sub-package it could lead to problems if we retain the same name. e.g. some plugins in mapview / leaflet.extras may not have been ported to 1.x, and ergo won't work with the latest leaflet package (if we were to retain the same name).

title: Leaflet 0.7.7 problem in internet explorer and edge
description:
Issue with leaflet/shiny in internet explorer and edge with github version of rstudio/leaflet

Reproducible example : leafletProxy example at https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/shiny.html

title: Caching issues when reloading WMSTiles
description:
Hi,

Thanks for this great package - I am using it in integration with Shiny and it does some real nice mapping!

That brings me to my question/issue:
I have a shinydashboard interface that allows the user to define some inputs and hit an actionButton, which then calls a layer in GeoServer and returns WMSTiles, which I add to leaflet using addWMSTiles(). However, it appears leaflet caches a particular set of WMSTiles once they've been displayed. For example, if I change the colour in GeoServer and then add the same WMSTiles as previously, the legend changes, but the actual WMSTiles in leaflet remain unchanged, only when I change the zoom level does it render the WMSTiles with the new colour scheme. It then caches this map for that zoom level and so once a map has been rendered for a specific zoom level, it always returns the cached version, as opposed to what I am actually calling.

This happens despite the fact that I am executing clearTiles() and clearImages() before every new addWMSTiles() call. It only happens when I do this in a browser (Chrome or IE), but not if I run it within the RStudio window. I am tempted to believe it has something to do with this: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/15048096/how-do-i-force-a-leaflet-map-to-reload-all-tiles-including-visible-ones

My JS is not good enough to implement that and I was wondering if something like this could be part of the leaflet R package.

Thanks

Bastian

Here's the relevant code snippet (sorry, I don't think I can make it reproducible w/o a WMS Server, e.g. GeoServer installed):

leafletProxy("map") %>% clearTiles() %>% clearImages() %>% setView(lng = view_def$lng, lat = view_def$lat, zoom = view_def$zoom) %>% addProviderTiles(paste0(input$basemap)) %>% addWMSTiles(
        paste0('http://localhost:8080/geoserver/Hail/wms?service=WMS&version=1.1.0&request=GetMap&format=image%2Fpng'),
        layers = "Hail1",
        options = WMSTileOptions(format = "image/png", opacity = 0.5,transparent = TRUE), #
        attribution = "")

title: Meta Issue for future development.
description:
## Leaflet past 1.1

Leaflet 1.1 releases is very near and this page is a mental note of what needs to be done past 1.1.
### Core Package

New Features and Upgrades
- [ ] Upgrade to [Leaflet JS 1.x](http://leafletjs.com/2016/09/27/leaflet-1.0-final.html).
  - Upgrading the JS lib is no big deal.
  - Making sure all plugins are 1.x compatible (including the ones in leaflet.extras) IS a big deal.
  - One option is to have a new package leaflet2
- [ ] Support [sf](https://github.com/edzer/sfr) data

Improvements
- [ ] Integrate Lodash and more functional Javascript.
- [ ] Split big JS and R files to more modular units. (layers.R, methods.JS are way too big right now).
- [ ] Babel-ify plugin glue javascript.
- [ ] Performance improvements for "big data". (Don't know what it means for now)
### [Leaflet.extras](https://github.com/bhaskarvk/leaflet.extras)
- No new plugins should be put in core leaflet package.
- Leaflet.extras will be the new repo for odds-n-end plugins.
- See [leaflet-extras Issue 6](https://github.com/bhaskarvk/leaflet.extras/issues/6) for a list of plugins 
### Add-on packages

These plugins should be independent packages as they are too big and complex.
- [ ] [Esri.Leaflet](https://github.com/Esri/esri-leaflet)
- [ ] [CartoDB](https://github.com/cartodb/cartodb.js)
- [ ] [Mapbox](https://github.com/mapbox/mapbox.js)
- [ ] [Mapbox GL](https://github.com/mapbox/mapbox-gl-leaflet)
- [ ] [PolarMap](https://github.com/GeoSensorWebLab/polarmap.js)
- [ ] [Mapzen-JS](https://mapzen.com/documentation/mapzen-js)
- [ ] [Tangram](https://mapzen.com/documentation/tangram/Javascript-API/)
- [ ] [Mapzen-Hoverboard](https://github.com/mapzen/hoverboard)
- [ ] [NASA GIBS](https://github.com/aparshin/leaflet-GIBS)

title: Adding a label tiles above paths
description:
Apologies for the repeat (or is this a continuation) of a [previously opened issue](https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/issues/218). 

I'd like to add a layer of tiles that renders on top of my basemap and path layers. This type of map is referred to [here](https://carto.com/blog/let-your-labels-shine/) as a "sandwich" map, and is illustrated in this [leaflet map](https://georgejosephatlantic.carto.com/viz/fc27f37e-75ca-11e6-933e-0e05a8b3e3d7/public_map).

@bhaskarvk [suggested](https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/issues/218#issuecomment-247685540) that this can be done by doing the following steps:

> a) add CartoDB.PositronNoLabels Tiles
> b) add your polygons with z-index < 1, so that the underly basemap tiles show a bit.
> c) add the CartoDB.PositronOnlyLabels Tiles with zIndex > 1 so they show above the other two layers.

However, I haven't been able to recreate this map "sandwich" despite my best efforts. Is there a way to set the zIndex of a path layer (e.g. polygons, circles, etc.)? If so, why isn't it a parameter in the `pathOptions` function?  Is there another way of achieving the desired effect of have unobstructed label tiles?

Here's what I've tried:

```
library(leaflet)

cities <- read.csv(textConnection("
City,Lat,Long,Pop
  Boston,42.3601,-71.0589,645966
  Hartford,41.7627,-72.6743,125017
  New York City,40.7127,-74.0059,8406000
  Philadelphia,39.9500,-75.1667,1553000
  Pittsburgh,40.4397,-79.9764,305841
  Providence,41.8236,-71.4222,177994
  "))

leaflet() %>%
        addTiles('http://{s}.basemaps.cartocdn.com/light_nolabels/{z}/{x}/{y}.png',options = tileOptions(zIndex = -1)) %>%
        addTiles('http://{s}.basemaps.cartocdn.com/light_only_labels/{z}/{x}/{y}.png',options = tileOptions(zIndex = 1000)) %>%
        addCircles(data = cities,lng = ~Long, lat = ~Lat, weight = 1,
                   radius = ~sqrt(Pop) * 30, fillOpacity = .85)
```

Many thanks,

Tiernan

title: The Incremental Stranglehold - Or Why leaflet::clearShapes() Can Slowly Render an Interactive Map Unusable
description:
[This issue in a single image ...](http://lowres.jantoo.com/animal-kingdom-snake-serpent-reptile-hug-boa_constrictor-12265271_low.jpg)

**Issue**
When creating a Shiny map with thousands of points, you start to hit a point where interactivity gets rather sluggish.  

A great way to improve performance is to dynamically add only those points which fall within the current map window.  Unfortunately - This does not work due to an underlying bug:  `clearShapes()` does not remove points already added.

Therefore, as users interact with the map and points are dynamically added, the old ones are never removed ... Thus the stranglehold towards sluggishness commences ...

**Show Me the Proof**
The best example of the issue and replication is likely RStudio's superZip dashboard:
- http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/superzip-example.html

Many others have come across this, as documented and replicated:
- http://stackoverflow.com/questions/31907805/leafletproxy-clearshapes-works-once-subsequently-data-dots-are-added-and-not
- https://groups.google.com/forum/?utm_medium=email&utm_source=footer#!msg/shiny-discuss/AFmWBWJCbsk/3a1Q_xdbFQAJ
- http://stackoverflow.com/questions/32107667/clearshapes-not-working-leaflet-for-r (This is a slightly different underlying cause it appears, yet susceptible to the same issue ...)

**How Important is This?**
Important.  The Shiny / Leaflet combination is incredible, and the potential for expansive geographic analysis groundbreaking.  Unfortunately, as long as this issue remains in effect there is an unnecessarily low and persistent limit on the number of points you can essentially work with.

**Are There Workarounds?**
Maybe.  Leveraging markers instead of points is a possibility as suggested in #246.  This isn't always what you're looking to accomplish with the geographic visualization however ...

**What If It Was Fixed Quickly?**
@jcheng5 @yihui - I'd send a pizza of your choice straight to your office!

Great work as always on Shiny / Leaflet!

```
polygon
    .on('dragstart', onDragStart)
    .on('drag',      onDrag)
    .on('dragend',   onDragEnd);
```

This is a minimum example to reproduce a draggble polygon.

Notes: You need to install  my fork if you would like to test the codes below.

```
library(leaflet)
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
    leafletOutput('map'),
    verbatimTextOutput('summary')
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

    output$summary <- renderPrint({
        event <- input$map_shape_click
        print(paste(paste(names(event), event, sep = '='), collapse = ', '))
    })

    output$map <- renderLeaflet({

        leaflet() %>% 
            addTiles() %>%
            addPolygons(
                lng = c(0, 10, 10, 0, 0),
                lat = c(0, 0, 10, 10, 0),
                options = pathOptions(draggable = TRUE),
                layerId = 'Polygon_1'
            )
    })
}


shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: FR: Geobuf / running JS on server
description:
An issue we have is the bandwidth required for users to receive large GeoJSON files (which works for points, polygons, lines, etc). There's a number of different solutions for this but it appears [Geobuf](https://github.com/mapbox/geobuf) is the best solution, particularly because it is being developed by the same developer as Leaflet. It's a lossless compression of GeoJSON into [Google Protocol Buffers](https://github.com/google/protobuf). It requires [pbf](https://github.com/mapbox/pbf). I have a test script with no issues in HTML/JS.

The client needs to run a function `var geojson = geobuf.decode(new Pbf(buffer));` which is simple enough in addGeoJSON. However, I'm having difficulty getting it encoded and sent in this format with JS on the server, ala `var buffer = geobuf.encode(statesData, new Pbf())`. I could possibly resort to using a separate node instance and use the command line, or use [pygeobuf](https://github.com/mapbox/pygeobuf) along with [rPython](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rPython/index.html). However, I suspect this would be an improvement for many folks.

Do you have any tips or thoughts on how I could integrate this? I noticed [RProtoBuf](https://github.com/eddelbuettel/rprotobuf) as well.

Chris

title: feature request: custom CRS support
description:
Hi, 

Leaflet supports only few projection out of the box. These projections (like WGS84) are mainly suitable to show a map of the entire world. A lot of use cases only require to show a map of a certain area (e.g. country, state, etc.). Depending on the latitude the standard projections can create maps that are very malformed (instead of what maps.google.com [suggests](https://www.google.nl/maps/@57.2632641,-123.949721,3.24z) Alaska [does not](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Map_of_USA_AK.svg/265px-Map_of_USA_AK.svg.png) represent ~30-35% of United States landmass). 

There is a JS library called [Proj4leaflet](http://kartena.github.io/Proj4Leaflet/) that extends on leaflet and adds supports for all major projections. It would be nice to have these available in leaflet for R. Proj4leaflet provides a branch for leaflet 0.7.x and for the 1.0 branch of leaflet (now in beta 2). Maybe a future switch to the 1.0 branch of leaflet ([issue 175](https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/issues/175)) could provide an opportunity to also support all major projections through proj4leaflet.

Unfortunately my JS skills are close to non-existent (which is the reason why i'm so happy with rstudio's shiny!) so i don't really know how to contribute myself. What are the plans on switching to leaflet 1.0? Are you waiting for a stable release of leaflet 1.0? 

Peter

title: Raster over international date line
description:
This issue was filed in mapview (https://github.com/environmentalinformatics-marburg/mapview/issues/6)

As mapview uses leaflet and this is a leaflet issue I reproduce it here.

This works fine:

``` r
library(raster)
r <- raster(xmn = 165, xmx = 180, ymn = -50, ymx = -31, crs = "+init=epsg:4326", nrows = 50, ncols = 50)
r[] <- rnorm(ncell(r))
leaflet() %>% addTiles() %>% addRasterImage(r)
```

But not this, with the raster being cropped and the cells being stretched:

``` r
r <- raster(xmn = 165, xmx = 185, ymn = -50, ymx = -31, crs = "+init=epsg:4326", nrows = 50, ncols = 50)
r[] <- rnorm(ncell(r))
leaflet() %>% addTiles() %>% addRasterImage(r)
```

Any idea how I can make this work?

Rotating the raster helps somewhat, but it would be nice for the raster to not be split into two parts at either end of the map (as is the case for polygons, see below).

``` r
r <- raster(xmn = 165, xmx = 185, ymn = -50, ymx = -31, crs = "+init=epsg:4326", nrows = 50, ncols = 50)
r[] <- rnorm(ncell(r))
leaflet() %>% addTiles() %>% addRasterImage(rotate(r))
```

There is no problem with polygons (ideally this is the behaviour we would want for ratsers too):

``` r
p <- SpatialPolygons(list(Polygons(list(Polygon(cbind(x=c(165, 165, 185, 185, 165),
                                                     y=c(-50, -31, -31, -50, -50)))), 1)),
                    proj4string=CRS("+init=epsg:4326"))
leaflet() %>% addTiles() %>% addPolygons(data = p)
```

Thanks in advance,
Tim

title: Feature Request: Add text (e.g. static labels) to map
description:
This request stems from another `leaflet` package user's  [question posted on Stackoverflow.](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/31745525/leaflet-with-r-add-text-labels)

I'd like to add static text labels to a leaflet map that I built and deployed with `shiny`. 

You can check it out here: [https://maynardandking.shinyapps.io/Census-Data-and-Leaflet-Map](https://maynardandking.shinyapps.io/Census-Data-and-Leaflet-Map)

And the code is available here: [https://github.com/tiernanmartin/Census-Data-and-Leaflet-Map/blob/master/app.R](https://github.com/tiernanmartin/Census-Data-and-Leaflet-Map/blob/master/app.R)

As you can see, I'm currently using the `leaflet` package's popup objects to label the counties. It sorta works, but I don't really like that there's a caption box around the text – it's eye-catching and it distracts the viewer from the main point of this choropleth: the color of the census tracts.

I also am not too happy with the way that the basemap's labels are blocked by the polygon layers. I know I could address this by adjusting the opacity of the polygon layer, but I'd prefer to leave the opacity as-is and add my own labels layer on top of the polygons.

Could you add a feature that allows text to be added to a location on the map _without using popups or markers_? I'm thinking of a function that is identical to `addPopups` except that it just displays the text and inherits styling from the map's .css file.

Thanks for the great package!

title: addPolylines does not support lines broken in several pieces
description:
This example has two lines identified separately in a `SpatialLines` object and it works

``` r
x1 <- SpatialLines(
  LinesList = list(
    Lines( slinelist=list( Line(cbind(c(5,6,7),c(43,44,45))) ), ID=1),
    Lines( slinelist=list( Line(cbind(c(8,9,9),c(43,44,45))) ), ID=2)
  )
)
leaflet() %>% addTiles() %>% addPolylines(data=x1)
```

Now with two pieces of a line with the same ID, `addPolylines` only shows the first piece.

``` r
x2 <- SpatialLines(
  LinesList = list(
    Lines( slinelist=list(
        Line(cbind(c(5,6,7),c(43,44,45))),
        Line(cbind(c(8,9,9),c(43,44,45)))
      ), ID=1
    )
  )
)
leaflet() %>% addTiles() %>% addPolylines(data=x2)
```

Getting pieces of lines is usual when computing them (using `rasterToContour` for example).

There is probably a way to convert from

``` r
leaflet:::polygonData.SpatialLinesDataFrame(x2)
```

to

``` r
leaflet:::polygonData.SpatialLinesDataFrame(x1)
```

But I am guessing there is probably something more clever to be done!

NB: given that the code is much of the same, I suspect this bug is also true for polygons which are composed of several sub-polygons.

title: FR: Raster Image RGB / multi layer support

I also tried to generate a color palette, which would map the "true" colors to the pixels, but had no success.

Is there currently a way to solve this problem?
It would be great, if RGB true color support was integrated in the `addRasterImage()` function.

title: Custom markers popup anchor point only used if popupAnchorX not equal to zero
description:
When defining a custom icon set to create markers that vary depending on the data, e.g.:

```
leafIcons <- icons(
  iconUrl = ifelse(quakes1$mag < 4.6,
    "http://leafletjs.com/docs/images/leaf-green.png",
    "http://leafletjs.com/docs/images/leaf-red.png"
  ),
  iconWidth = 38, iconHeight = 95,
  iconAnchorX = 22, iconAnchorY = 94,
  shadowUrl = "http://leafletjs.com/docs/images/leaf-shadow.png",
  shadowWidth = 50, shadowHeight = 64,
  shadowAnchorX = 4, shadowAnchorY = 62
)
```

to control the anchoring of the popup window, two more parameters are supported, popupAnchorX and popupAnchorY.  These are offsets from the iconAnchor coordinates, so a typical usage would be

```
popupAnchorX = 0,  popupAnchorY = -40
```

However, these params are not used unless popupAnchorX is something other than zero.  The code that checks to see if these are set should be fixed.

title: CRS bug
description:
Hi,

if you try to change CRS using WMSTileOptions you'll get a javascript error:
`Uncaught TypeError: this._crs.project is not a function`

Function _this._crs.project_ is defined in _leaflet-src.js_ in function _onAdd_.

Example without crs defined (works):

``` r
leaflet() %>% setView(-93.65, 42.0285, zoom = 4) %>%
  addWMSTiles(
    "http://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/wms/nexrad/n0r.cgi",
    layers = "nexrad-n0r-900913",
    options = WMSTileOptions(format = "image/png", transparent = TRUE))
```

Example with crs defined (does not work)

``` r
leaflet() %>% setView(-93.65, 42.0285, zoom = 4) %>%
  addWMSTiles(
    "http://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/wms/nexrad/n0r.cgi",
    layers = "nexrad-n0r-900913",
    options = WMSTileOptions(format = "image/png", transparent = TRUE, crs="EPSG:4326"))
```

Please note that map is already using epsg:4326 so first and second example should have same result.

        clearMarkers() %>%
        clearControls() %>%
        addCircleMarkers(fillOpacity = 0.9,
                         lng = ~longitude, 
                         lat = ~latitude, 
                         layerId = ~loc,
                         stroke = FALSE, 
                         color = ~pal(m),

```

I know I am resetting GAdata() properly overall based on the inputs because this solves my problem:

```

    leafletProxy("mymap", data = GAdata()) %>%
            clearMarkers() %>%

title: [feature request] setStyle (dynamic styles without resending entire Vector layers)
Leafletproxy error with Shiny server
description:
Hi, 

A couple of days ago I asked this question in the Shiny discuss forum but I did not get any answers. Maybe, I have more luck here as I don't even know where to start to debug the problem. 

I have copied and pasted this example from the RStudio Leaftet page. It works fine running locally (runApp) but the JS explodes if I run it via Shiny server. As far as I can tell, it does not like the leafletProxy call. 

ui.R is as follows:

```
library(shiny)
library(leaflet)
library(RColorBrewer)

bootstrapPage(
  tags$style(type = "text/css", "html, body {width:100%;height:100%}"),
  leafletOutput("map", width = "100%", height = "100%"),
  absolutePanel(top = 10, right = 10,
                sliderInput("range", "Magnitudes", min(quakes$mag), max(quakes$mag),
                            value = range(quakes$mag), step = 0.1
                ),
                selectInput("colors", "Color Scheme",
                            rownames(subset(brewer.pal.info, category %in% c("seq", "div")))
                ),
                checkboxInput("legend", "Show legend", TRUE)
  )
)
```

server.R is as follows:

```
server <- function(input, output, session) {

  # Reactive expression for the data subsetted to what the user selected
  filteredData <- reactive({
    quakes[quakes$mag >= input$range[1] & quakes$mag <= input$range[2],]
  })

  # This reactive expression represents the palette function,
  # which changes as the user makes selections in UI.
  colorpal <- reactive({
    colorNumeric(input$colors, quakes$mag)
  })

  output$map <- renderLeaflet({
    # Use leaflet() here, and only include aspects of the map that
    # won't need to change dynamically (at least, not unless the
    # entire map is being torn down and recreated).
    leaflet(quakes) %>% addTiles() %>%
      fitBounds(~min(long), ~min(lat), ~max(long), ~max(lat))
  })

  # Incremental changes to the map (in this case, replacing the
  # circles when a new color is chosen) should be performed in
  # an observer. Each independent set of things that can change
  # should be managed in its own observer.
  observe({
    pal <- colorpal()

    leafletProxy("map", data = filteredData()) %>%
      clearShapes() %>%
      addCircles(radius = ~10^mag/10, weight = 1, color = "#777777",
                 fillColor = ~pal(mag), fillOpacity = 0.7, popup = ~paste(mag)
      )
  })

  # Use a separate observer to recreate the legend as needed.
  observe({
    proxy <- leafletProxy("map", data = quakes)

    # Remove any existing legend, and only if the legend is
    # enabled, create a new one.
    proxy %>% clearControls()
    if (input$legend) {
      pal <- colorpal()
      proxy %>% addLegend(position = "bottomright",
                          pal = pal, values = ~mag
      )
    }
  })
}
```

Everything runs fine locally but I get a very non-descriptive error if I run the app via shiny server which seems to point to leafletProxy as the source of the error:

```
Listening on http://127.0.0.1:55286
Warning: Unhandled error in observer: wrong arguments for subsetting an environment
observe({
    pal <- colorpal()
    leafletProxy("map", data = filteredData()) %>% clearShapes() %>%
        addCircles(radius = ~10^mag/10, weight = 1, color = "#777777",
            fillColor = ~pal(mag), fillOpacity = 0.7, popup = ~paste(mag))
})
```

Any ideas what might be causing the problem? I am using the same machine to run locally and via Shiny server.

Thanks,

Carlos

title: Is is possible to Customize the Clustered Markers?
Points/polygons/polylines should be reverse-projected
description:
From the tutorial materials here:

http://www.uclm.es/profesorado/vgomez/useR2015/

``` r
BMcD <- readOGR("datasets/BMcD.shp", "BMcD")
leaflet(BMcD) %>% addTiles() %>% addMarkers()
```

This ought to work but doesn't, due to `BMcD` using a non-WGS84 projection. The CRS info is included on the `BMcD` object, though, so we should do the conversion automatically. Here is a manual way:

``` r
coords <- rgdal::project(BMcD@coords, BMcD@proj4string@projargs, inv = TRUE)
```

title: colorQuantile function requires refining to decide quantiles when data is not well distributed
description:
Hi there,

First of all thank you very much for the efforts to develop leaflet for R!

Recently I encountered an issue when trying to decide quantiles for data when coloring the map. The data is not well distributed so it cannot even select 9 quantiles in 306 values. Here is the code.

``` R
> vals
  [1]   2   0   2 127   2   3   1   8   7   3   4  16   3   5   4   6   1   3   5   1   1   4   4   1  11   1   0   1   3   2   3   7  14   2   9  16   1   6   5   4   3   5  10   8   7   4   0
 [48]  11   5   4   7   3   2   8   1   3   4   3   3  21  11   6   2  10   5   5   2   2   5   2   5  10  27   0   5   9   6   6   5   4  20   7   4   6   8   3   5  20   4   2   8   3   7  10
 [95]   1   8   7   2   1   9   2   5 137   4   3   0   3   5   6   7   2  17   4   4   4   4   3   2   0   2   5   1   0   3   1   2   0  10  12   3   7   5   0  11   5   4   2   2   1   0   4
[142]   6   2   3   2   7   6   2   1   5   1   9   2   0   4   0   7   3   4   4   0   0   1   0   5   8   1   2   4  10  12  15   2   5   3   2   3   1   5   0   7  67   1   2   5   1   2   0
[189]   3   6   1   7   2   1   4   2   2   8   0   3   3   7   3  16   8   6  18   2  20   5   3  28   2   6   5   5   6   1  10   2  18   7   5   7   8   6   6   7   7  10   4  17   6  12   5
[236]   5   4   4   3   6   8   2   2   0   7   6   4   3   4   4   6   3  39   4   2   1   3   2   3   1   0   6   6   0   4   1  14  13   0  25   2   4   5   5  11   2   2   0  17   6   2   3
[283]   5   7   1   4   3   2  19   2   2   6   1   1   2   1   2   1   1   4   3   0   4   3
> pal <- colorQuantile("YlOrRd", NULL, n = 9)
> pal(vals)
Error in cut.default(x, binsToUse, labels = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE,  : 
  'breaks' are not unique
```

Then I looked into the source code of _colorQuantile_ function and tried to debug it step by step.

``` R
> probs <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 10)
> probs
 [1] 0.0000000 0.1111111 0.2222222 0.3333333 0.4444444 0.5555556 0.6666667 0.7777778 0.8888889 1.0000000
> bins <- quantile(vals, probs, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
> bins
 [1]   0   1   2   2   3   4   5   7  10 137
```

So this is the reason! There are 2 same quantiles causing the problem in cut. If I decrease the number of quantile to 8, then there won't be any problem. However, based on different filter criteria, query results cannot be predicted so it is difficult to predefine the number of quantiles. So what I am doing is as follows:

``` R
      probs <- seq(0, 1, length.out = quantileNum + 1)
      bins <- quantile(newObsVal, probs, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
      while (length(unique(bins)) != length(bins)) {
        quantileNum <- quantileNum - 1
        probs <- seq(0, 1, length.out = quantileNum + 1)
        bins <- quantile(newObsVal, probs, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
      }
```

It looks quite ugly and may lead to performance issues, but it works. After some investigation, I also discovered that it seems we can also use _.bincode_ to categorize data:

``` R
> bins
 [1]   0   1   2   2   3   4   5   7  10 137
> .bincode(vals, bins, include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE)
  [1] 4 1 4 9 4 5 2 8 8 5 6 9 5 7 6 7 2 5 7 2 2 6 6 2 9 2 1 2 5 4 5 8 9 4 8 9 2 7 7 6 5 7 9 8 8 6 1 9 7 6 8 5 4 8 2 5 6 5 5 9 9 7 4 9 7 7 4 4 7 4 7 9 9 1 7 8 7 7 7 6 9 8 6 7 8 5 7 9 6 4 8 5 8 9
 [95] 2 8 8 4 2 8 4 7 9 6 5 1 5 7 7 8 4 9 6 6 6 6 5 4 1 4 7 2 1 5 2 4 1 9 9 5 8 7 1 9 7 6 4 4 2 1 6 7 4 5 4 8 7 4 2 7 2 8 4 1 6 1 8 5 6 6 1 1 2 1 7 8 2 4 6 9 9 9 4 7 5 4 5 2 7 1 8 9 2 4 7 2 4 1
[189] 5 7 2 8 4 2 6 4 4 8 1 5 5 8 5 9 8 7 9 4 9 7 5 9 4 7 7 7 7 2 9 4 9 8 7 8 8 7 7 8 8 9 6 9 7 9 7 7 6 6 5 7 8 4 4 1 8 7 6 5 6 6 7 5 9 6 4 2 5 4 5 2 1 7 7 1 6 2 9 9 1 9 4 6 7 7 9 4 4 1 9 7 4 5
[283] 7 8 2 6 5 4 9 4 4 7 2 2 4 2 4 2 2 6 5 1 6 5
```

So maybe we can replace _cut_ with _.bincode_? However I don't know if there is any other side-effect. If we should not, what can I do to get around this issue?

Thank you very much and have a nice day.

Regards,
Yang

title: Feature Request: Better Default Handling of Color
description:
Hi Rstudio Team,

Thanks for your great work on this package. 

I'd like to request a feature to allow default color handling for any column name that is passed via the scripting interface. Right now the `color` argument works well when there is a string, a vector of colors, or a dataframe column of colors. However if you simply pass the name of any old column `leaflet` cannot handle the data. To me, a best-guess representation of color in the spirit of `ggplot` is desirable where leaflet can detect if the column is a string, a categorical variable, or a continuous variable. 

``` [R]
library(leaflet)

#dataframe with lat/lon and a categorical and continuous variable
df = data.frame(Lat = 1:10, 
                Long = rnorm(10),
                CatVar = sample(c("A","B","C"), 10, replace = T),
                ConVar = rnorm(10))

#basemap
m = leaflet(df) %>% addTiles()

# these work
m %>% addCircles(color="red")
m %>% addCircles(color = topo.colors(10,alpha = NULL ))

#it would be great for these to have defaults as well
m %>% addCircles(color=~CatVar)
m %>% addCircles(color=~ConVar)
```

thanks,
zach cp

title: How many bins in colorBin?
description:
I'm working with the feature/color-legend branch.
I use colorBin with unemployment data. This is the code:

``` R
colorBin('YlOrRd', leedsShape@data$Unemployed_, bins= 5 ,na.color = "#808080")
...
attr(,"colorArgs")$bins
[1]  0  2  4  6  8 10 12 14
```

If I use `bins=5`  I get 8 bins.  I get 8 bins with `bins=6` all the way to  `bins=8`.
`bins=9`  gives 13!  (the 'YlOrRd' palette gets up to 9 colours).

If I use `bins=4` I get four bins:

``` R
colorBin('YlOrRd', leedsShape@data$Unemployed_, bins= 4 ,na.color = "#808080")
...
attr(,"colorArgs")$bins
[1]  0  5 10 15 
```

As `leedsShape@data$Unemployed_,` is the vector with the actual data (including NA) I've tried to give the domain as a range ( `0:12.83` or `c(0, 12.83`).

Using `domain= c(0,12.83)`:
If I use `bins=4` I get four bins.  I get 8 bins with `bins=6` all the way to  `bins=8`.
Using `domain= 0:12.83`:
If I use `bins=4` I get four bins.  I get 7 bins with `bins=6` all the way to  `bins=8`.

title: Discard the raw data passed to leaflet() when converting everything to JSON?
description:
This is really an htmlwidgets issue. I guess we do not really need to carry the raw data to the HTML page, e.g. for

```
leaflet(data = df) %>% addTiles() %>% addCircles(~lat, ~lng, color = ~color)
```

The result will be `list(data = df, tileLayer = ..., circle = list(lat, lng, list(color = ...))`. The whole thing is converted to JSON and inserted in HTML, but this may be of concern when df is relatively large and we do not really need it to be converted to JSON. So we may need a way for htmlwidgets::createWidget() to discard certain elements from `x`.
